sectionsContent.title: Distance, Displacement & Average Velocity

concept.summary: Distance is how far you travelled; displacement is how far you ended up from where you started. Distance is a scalar and never negative. Displacement is a vector — it carries a sign, and the sign is meaningless until you say which way is positive.
keyIdeas: Speed pairs with distance. Velocity pairs with displacement. They are not interchangeable words.
A round trip has real distance and zero displacement, so it has real average speed and zero average velocity.
State your positive direction before you write a single number.

items: Scientific notation and significant figures (U0 S0.2).
Rearranging an equation for the variable you want (U0 S0.3).
Reading a value off a number line, including negative positions.

sectionsContent.directions: Work every problem in your Hayden-McNeil notebook. Number each one, show the givens, and carry units the whole way through. Bring the sheet and your notebook to class.

questions.prompt: A skateboarder pushes off and rolls 5 m east down the sidewalk, then coasts 3 m farther east before rolling to a stop. Find the total distance travelled and the displacement.
A motorcycle courier covers 120 km of city deliveries in 2.0 hours. Find the average speed in km/h.
An e-bike rider covers 90 km on a single charge over a 3.0-hour ride. Find her average speed in km/h.
A delivery drone flies 200 m east from the warehouse, then has to backtrack 50 m west around a tree. Find the total distance travelled and the displacement.
A zip-line rider starts at x = 10 m and reaches x = 70 m along the cable in 20 s. Find the displacement and the average velocity.
A hoverboard rider glides 8 m north across the gym floor, then glides 8 m south back to the starting line, taking 10 s in total. Find the total distance, the displacement, and the average velocity.
parts: Before you calculate: which of those three will be zero, and why?

questions.prompt: A kayaker paddles from x = 5 m to x = −15 m along the shoreline in 10 s. Find the displacement and the average velocity.
A cyclist starts at x₀ = −15 m, rides forward to x = 50 m, then backtracks to a final position of 40 m, all in 25 s. Find the total distance travelled and the average velocity.
An e-bike's speedometer displays an average velocity of 3.4 m/s. Convert it to km/h and express your answer with the correct number of significant figures (U0 S0.2).
parts: Then say in one sentence why 3.4 m/s and 12.24 km/h are not equally honest answers.
